hypotheses.observation: Extending the live set from 116 to 144 registers per thread exceeds the 128-register residency budget, causing 22.0 GB/s of local spills and reducing occupancy from 0.50 to 0.0625.
hypotheses.mechanism: Register pressure crosses the residency threshold, so preserving the row input across the reduction triggers spilling and severe occupancy loss.
hypotheses.transformation: Do not keep the immutable row input live across the reduction; reload or rematerialize it at the second use site.
preconditions: The row input remains unchanged between use sites.
Reloading or rematerializing produces bitwise-equivalent values for the reference dtype.
The added load or recomputation cost is lower than the spill and occupancy cost.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Keep the live set at or below the residency budget, eliminating or materially reducing spills and preserving higher occupancy.
risks: Additional memory traffic or recomputation may offset residency gains.
Rematerialization may alter numerical results if it changes evaluation order.
unknowns: Whether the input can be cheaply reloaded from the relevant cache or memory level.
required_evidence: Measure the live-set and spill rate for a reload/rematerialization variant.
Verify bitwise equivalence at both use sites.

hypotheses.observation: The same immutable row input is used before and after a reduction, while one row maps to one thread block.
hypotheses.mechanism: A phase boundary can shorten per-thread liveness, but separating phases may introduce launch, synchronization, or intermediate-storage costs.
hypotheses.transformation: Evaluate a two-phase implementation with the reduction and post-reduction use separated, retaining only the necessary intermediate result between phases.
preconditions: The intermediate result can be represented without exceeding the residency budget.
The phase boundary preserves the required operation ordering and bitwise-equivalent output.
Kernel-launch and intermediate-storage overheads are acceptable.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Reduce register lifetime across the reduction and avoid the spill regime, potentially restoring occupancy toward the measured pre-extension level.
risks: Extra kernel launch and global-memory traffic may dominate.
A changed reduction or synchronization structure may violate bitwise equivalence.
unknowns: The size and cost of the required intermediate state.
Whether the reduction result can be transferred without changing numerical behavior.
Actual performance after accounting for launch and memory overhead.
required_evidence: Measure end-to-end time, register use, spills, and occupancy for the separated phases.
Compare outputs bitwise with the reference dtype.

hypotheses.observation: The measured extension past the residency budget causes a large occupancy collapse and local spilling.
hypotheses.mechanism: Register caching of the row input across both use sites is not beneficial when it raises the live set above the budget.
hypotheses.transformation: Defer or reject any transformation that extends the live set to 144 registers per thread unless a measurement shows that its reuse benefit outweighs spill and occupancy costs.
preconditions: The measured spill and occupancy behavior is representative of the target launch configuration.
No compensating reduction in other live values is introduced.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Avoid the known high-risk residency trap and preserve the current residency regime until a lower-live-set alternative is validated.
risks: A conservative choice may miss a benefit under a different launch configuration.
The existing 116-register baseline may still have other bottlenecks.
unknowns: Whether another transformation can reduce the live set enough to make input retention safe.
Whether the spill behavior changes with workload shape or launch parameters.
required_evidence: Measure representative workloads and launch configurations before considering deliberate live-set extension.
Quantify reuse savings against spill bandwidth and occupancy loss.
